items.title: Alonso's grid penalty grows to 30 places after a fourth exceeded PU element in FP3
items.summary: The Technical Delegate's Document 33 (25 September, 12:43) reports Aston Martin fitted Fernando Alonso's car with a new energy store unit during FP3 — his 7th of the 3 allowed for the season, a fourth element over his allocation for this event. The Stewards' Document 34 imposes a further 5-place grid penalty on top of the already-confirmed 25-place Document 20 ruling, taking Alonso's cumulative grid penalty for the Azerbaijan Grand Prix to 30 places. Lance Stroll's separately confirmed 20-place penalty (Document 21) for exceeding his own allocation is unchanged. Both remain subject to Article B2.5.4b.iv grid allocation if the car is classified in Qualifying. Elsewhere, the Stewards ruled (Document 19) that Valtteri Bottas's FP1 overtake of Albon under a yellow flag warranted no penalty, and the Turn 19 FP2 impeding investigation (Documents 22–23, summonses for Hamilton and Lawson) is resolved: Document 29 gives Lewis Hamilton (Car 44) a driving reprimand for impeding Liam Lawson's Car 30, with no separate ruling published against Lawson's own summons.
items.why_it_matters: A 30-place penalty exceeds the entire field, so Alonso will start last regardless of his qualifying position — removing any incentive to push for grid position in Qualifying and reshaping how Aston Martin approaches the session and the race strategy that follows. The Bottas ruling also sets a practical precedent for how tightly-timed yellow-flag overtakes are judged this weekend.

items.title: Verstappen tops FP3, denying Russell a clean sweep of Friday practice
items.summary: Max Verstappen set a 1:43.922 in the closing minutes of FP3 to finish one-tenth clear of George Russell and Lewis Hamilton, after brushing the walls several times on his fastest lap. Russell had led for most of the session; Kimi Antonelli was fourth. Charles Leclerc was best of the rest in fifth. Lance Stroll's session ended early after clipping the Turn 1 wall and damaging a wheel.
items.why_it_matters: Verstappen's late improvement breaks Russell's run of topping both Friday sessions and gives Red Bull a form marker heading into qualifying, on a track where practice pace has not always translated directly into grid position.

items.title: Hadjar returns to Red Bull for Baku after signing a 2027 extension
items.summary: Hadjar returns after missing Zandvoort, Monza and Madrid with a wrist fracture and has renewed with Red Bull for 2027. He says the simulator test went well but expects some continuing pain. Lawson returns to Racing Bulls and Tsunoda reverts to reserve.
items.why_it_matters: Baku's confirmed Red Bull/Racing Bulls line-up is the regular Verstappen-Hadjar pairing plus Lawson at Racing Bulls; do not carry the previous replacement chain into session results or teammate comparisons.

items.title: Williams brings its long-awaited FW48 upgrade package to Baku
items.summary: Formula1.com and The Race report that Williams is bringing its delayed FW48 package to Azerbaijan. Vowles told Formula1.com after Friday practice that it is 'a step in the right direction but not enough'; Albon and Sainz had earlier cautioned it may not deliver the full gain calculated months ago while the midfield continued to develop.
items.why_it_matters: This is a round-specific upgrade now tested in real practice conditions, not just a pre-weekend expectation — the team's own post-FP2 verdict tempers the pre-race optimism.
